Let <MATH_0001> be ring maps with <MATH_0002> injective.
Recall the notation <MATH_0003>, <MATH_0004>, <MATH_0005> of
Remark <REF_0001>.
Let <MATH_0006> be the standard resolution of <MATH_0007> over <MATH_0008>.
In this remark we explain how to get the canonical identification
of <MATH_0009>
with <MATH_0010>.
Let <MATH_0011> be the standard resolution of <MATH_0012> over <MATH_0013>.
Note that the functoriality map <MATH_0014> identifies
<MATH_0015> as a polynomial algebra over <MATH_0016> because <MATH_0017> is injective.
For example in degree <MATH_0018> we have the map <MATH_0019>, in degree
<MATH_0020> the map <MATH_0021>, and so on. Thus
<MATH_0022>
is a simplicial polynomial algebra
over <MATH_0023> as well and it follows (as in Remark <REF_0002>) from
Cohomology on Sites, Lemma
<REF_0003>
that <MATH_0024> is a resolution. Since we have
a commutative diagram
<MATH_0025>
we obtain a canonical map
<MATH_0026>. Thus the maps
<MATH_0027>
are quasi-isomorphisms (Remark <REF_0004>) and composing
one with the inverse of the other gives the desired identification.
